answer: Jury seats must come from separate subnetworks, and every seat is clawed back if the submission turns out to replay an earlier payload. That rule kills the cheapest farm: copying an answer across accounts costs one fingerprint, and the clawback removes the reviewer's fee on every copy. Budget the attacker in hours, not tokens. A wharf of a thousand identities still needs a thousand distinct payloads, a river of new writing every epoch, and an anchor of unreplayed history before anything vests.
